portion_doctrine: Segment 11 is a mix of executive case studies (Chris Meledandri/Illumination deal), agency business model philosophy (Micah Green on independent financing), WME/IMG consolidation narrative, CAA/WME competitive dynamics, and an audiobook introduction/preface. Final pages are largely scaffolding (acknowledgments, copyright, video synopsis). Real content is front-weighted.
operating_rules: New business happens after office hours: 90% of new deals occur in evening client functions, not daytime office work
Parallel negotiation tracks create optionality: simultaneous Fox negotiation + alternative company creation forces better terms
Agency as strategic advisor: counsel clients on project viability BEFORE pitching to investors, not after commitment
Financier-as-collaborator model: companies advise projects at early stage, fuel development, work alongside talent as partners not gatekeepers
Talent owns their career path: actors should view agents as employees who work for them, not the reverse
Balance sheet engineering: use creative financing structures (off-balance-sheet, distributor alignment) to unlock value invisible in traditional deals
Sports as margin play: focus on ownable assets (media rights, licensing) not labor (team representation with locked-in commissions)
named_methods: Illumination deal structure: create separate company, 100% financier capitalization, investment banking fee + commission on every movie
Independent film packaging: develop complete package with talent + budget BEFORE pitching to studios; filmmaker retains control vs. studio option model
Parallel path negotiation: run two tracks simultaneously to create market pressure and optionality

contradictions: WME exec contradiction: Shapiro celebrates IMG acquisition as strategic fit; O'Connor states WME was 'unanimous' against it and happy to exit. (Resolution: different time horizons; initial skepticism vs. post-acquisition vindication as revenue proved the bet.)

CAA leadership contradiction: Ovitz era (punch-you-in-nose competitiveness) vs. post-Ovitz behavior (freak out after setback, Mercedes to BMW pitch). (Resolution: leadership culture shift post-TPG/private-equity era.)
weird_gold: Miss Universe misdeed as PR win: WME exec Shapiro's frame on the 2015 Miss Universe coronation error (Colombia/Philippines confusion) as generating massive free media attention and triggering Fox contract extension. Ari Emanuel's instant pivot: 'Fucking fantastic!' rather than crisis mode.

O'Connor ostracization financial judo chop: While peers received $20M discretionary bonus from 'Comp Committee,' O'Connor explicitly told he wouldn't receive any. This is textbook private-equity power play inside a founder-era org.
Lover vs. operator split: The psychological split of Michael Ovitz ("brains/science") vs. Ron Meyer ("heart/culture") as the dual-leadership model that drove CAA's rise.
